hypothesis: The eight-hour soft boundary with extension only under continued regime support may reduce HYPE breakout giveback while allowing supported trends to continue toward the 24-hour hard boundary.
decision: Record the first fully resolved live soft-boundary decision without changing the active v14 contract. The HYPE short was closed at eight hours because its measured structure-alignment score was negative and below the extension threshold. The close limited an already adverse lifecycle, but one loss cannot establish that the boundary outperforms either an earlier exit or a longer hold. Continue prospective outcome and post-exit markout collection before revising the exit controller.
falsifier: The soft-boundary hypothesis is weakened if prospective post-exit paths repeatedly recover enough to outperform the actual close after additional funding and friction, or if supported extensions repeatedly lose more than immediate closes. It is strengthened only provisionally if non-overlapping live decisions show opposed structure exits reducing after-cost losses and supported extensions preserving after-cost gains.
limitations: One resolved decision cannot estimate the exit policy's expected value, drawdown effect, or regime-conditional reliability.
The audit has no completed post-exit counterfactual for this lifecycle, so it cannot establish whether holding longer would have recovered or worsened the loss.
The structure score is descriptive telemetry from the implemented rule, not an independently validated forecast.
The v11 current-run HYPE sample contained two losses and is too small to separate entry quality from exit quality.
No strategy, position, order, sizing policy, execution scope, or running process changed in this revision.
